name: FastAccounting
shortBlurb: Expense classification, forecasting and anomaly detection on Tally daybook data.
tagline: Party-group classification at 95.9% accuracy across 5 companies' books.
description: A proof of concept on 5 companies' Tally exports: Random Forest models with text features classify transactions by party and expense group (95.9% average party-group accuracy), XGBoost and Prophet forecast recurring expenses 3 months ahead, and Isolation Forest flags unusual entries for review.

name: CallMind
shortBlurb: Audit every call for script compliance automatically, instead of sampling a handful by hand.
tagline: Script-compliance scoring for call audio, without manual listening.
description: A GPU-accelerated pipeline that transcribes Hindi calls, separates speakers and scores each call against its campaign script, using a mix of multilingual embeddings and lexical matching. Raw audio becomes a structured compliance report for every call.

name: NextSurge Momentum Alpha
shortBlurb: Market-signal models built on engineered features and walk-forward validation.
tagline: Tested market signals built from robust feature engineering.
description: Feature-rich market-signal models with walk-forward testing.

name: JNVessays
shortBlurb: Handwriting-OCR pipeline for exam and evaluation workflow.
tagline: Extracts meaningful text from handwritten exam sheets.

name: DocIntel
shortBlurb: Document-understanding for PDFs, scans, and mixed-format files.
description: OCR and layout intelligence for complex documents.

name: GradeQP
shortBlurb: Checks draft question papers against paper-setting rules and cites the rule behind each finding.
tagline: Deterministic checks for exact form, an LLM for the judgement rules, and every finding traced to its source.
description: A proof of concept that parses a draft paper, extracts its structure in one structured LLM call, then runs deterministic checks and LLM-judged rules against a course-specific rulebook. The output is a verdict, findings that cite their rule, and a copy of the faculty member's own Word file with comments on the affected questions.
challenges: Rules spread across scheme, course and template files
Mixing exact form checks with LLM judgement

name: Report Copilot
shortBlurb: Plain-language report requests turned into rule-based, validated scripts over pseudonymised warehouse data.
tagline: LLM-written report scripts that only ever see schemas, never personal data.
description: A reporting system for an education non-profit's teacher programme. A plain-language request such as "training report for one state, split by district" is turned into business rules and a report script by an LLM, run against the warehouse, and the output is checked against the manual report on counts and values. The LLM only ever sees table schemas, never row values; 1,763 columns across 95 tables are classified for personal data, and direct identifiers are pseudonymised with a keyed HMAC-SHA256 hash, failing closed on any unclassified column.
dataTypes: Manual Power BI reports for validation
mlMethods: LLM-generated report scripts from plain-language requests
Business rules encoded and tested as code
Automated report validation against manual reports
challenges: Personal and child data under the DPDP Act
Business rules spread across manual reports
Proving automated reports match manual ones

name: Valent
shortBlurb: Cap-table and liquidation-waterfall extraction, with every value tied to a verbatim citation.
tagline: Source-cited preference terms, checked by a validator and confirmed by a reviewer before compute.
description: Valent extracts preference terms from US certificates of incorporation and Indian articles of association, with each value tied to a verbatim quote that a validator checks. A reviewer confirms every term, and the waterfall engine distributes an assumed exit value down the preference stack, with totals reconciled back to the exit value. The output distributes an assumed exit value. It does not estimate fair market value, which needs an EV-to-equity bridge and a locked valuation date.
dataTypes: Articles of association (text PDF, XFA forms, scanned PDFs)
mlMethods: LLM structured extraction (gpt-4o-mini via OpenRouter, Ollama fallback)
Clause indexing and keyword clause selection
challenges: Seniority and pari-passu ranking, which current models get wrong

name: Contract Risk Radar
shortBlurb: Three-stage LLM pipeline that checks cybersecurity contract clauses against 133 policy obligations and flags them for review.
tagline: Clause-level contract review grounded in past SME verdicts, with a rationale for every flag.
description: A three-stage pipeline (obligation extraction, per-obligation judgment, verdict prediction by analogy) reviews contract clauses against obligations drawn from three policy documents. Each flagged clause gets a verdict (Accept, Modify, Replace, Reject or Escalate), a confidence flag and a rationale, and low-similarity clauses default to Escalate. Built and evaluated on synthetic contracts.
dataTypes: Clause-level SME review verdicts and comments
mlMethods: LLM structured extraction with Pydantic schemas
Batched LLM judgment (10 obligations per call)
challenges: Clauses with no close precedent in the example set
Overlapping policy obligations from three source documents
Only 38 labelled SME examples to learn from
Choosing between escalate and modify when few close precedents exist

name: Farm Wildlife Alerts
shortBlurb: Night-time farm intrusion identification, with each species benchmarked on its own.
tagline: Species calls for farm wildlife, with false-alert exposure reported next to accuracy.
description: In development: a research-stage system that identifies which animal is entering a farm plot, built on pretrained wildlife detectors and classifiers. Each benchmark run scores every species on its own and reports how often a non-target animal would wake the farmer, next to accuracy. The night-time head, the alert logic and the field hardware are still being designed.
dataTypes: Public wildlife photographs and camera-trap archive images
Negative-class images: livestock, dogs, people, empty frames
mlMethods: Pretrained wildlife detector and species classifier, benchmarked per species
challenges: Night imagery is scarce in public archives
Look-alike animals in darkness (cattle and nilgai)
Keeping false alerts low enough that a farmer keeps the system on
Labels that do not match the animal in frame
